status: outcomes from KICD's text, word for word; skills, prerequisites and misconceptions not yet mapped

content_topics: Characteristics of plants as living things.
Functions of external parts of plants.
learning_experiences: search for information from print and non-print materials on characteristics of plants as living things and discuss with peers,
take a walk in the school compound and adjacent environment to observe, discuss and record evidence that plants: grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes in their environment and die
observe young plants/seedlings, draw and label their parts and share with peers (roots, stems and leaves),
discuss the functions of external parts of plants and share with peers,
use digital applications to draw, paint and label external parts of a plant.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are plants grouped as living things?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and Collaboration: The learner develops speaking and listening skills as they discuss the functions of external parts of plants.
Digital literacy: The learner develops manipulative skills as they interact with digital media to draw, paint and label external parts of a plant.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: The learner cooperates in taking turns while they observe young plants/seedlings, draw and label their parts and share with peers.
Respect: The learner listens to and appreciates others’ opinions during discussions on the characteristics of plants.
sub_strands.pcis: Safety and Security: The learner observes safety while handling different types of plants as they take a walk in the school compound and adjacent environment to observe, discuss and record characteristics of plants as living things.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner uses information on characteristics of plants as living things in the study of different types of crops.
sub_strands.design_notes: observes safety while handling different types of plants,

outcomes.text: identify characteristics of plants as living things
describe functions of external parts of plants
appreciate the need to care for plants

content_topics: Characteristics of animals as living things.
Vertebrates and invertebrates.
learning_experiences: take a walk in the school compound and adjacent environment to observe, discuss and record evidence that animals: feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond to changes in their environment and die,
search for information from print and non-print materials on characteristics of animals as living things and discuss the findings with peers,
search for information from print and non-print materials on main differences between vertebrates and invertebrates and share with peers,
take a walk in the school compound and immediate environment to identify vertebrates and invertebrates in their locality.
key_inquiry_questions: Why are animals grouped as living things?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: The learner contributes to group decision making by participating actively as they discuss characteristics of animals as living things.
Creativity and Imagination: The learner discovers new ways of solving problems of keeping records as they design and make a portfolio of vertebrates and invertebrates.
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: The learner takes care of the different materials they use as they search for information from print and non-print materials on main differences between vertebrates and invertebrates and share with peers.
Respect: The learner appreciates divergent ideas from peers as they discuss their findings on characteristics of animals as living things.
sub_strands.pcis:
Animal welfare: The learner takes care of animals during the learning activities.
Safety and security: The learner observes safety when handling animals.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner uses the information on characteristics of animals as living things in the study of livestock.
sub_strands.design_notes: Learners observe safety precautions and take care of animals during the learning activities.

outcomes.text: identify the characteristics of animals as living things
distinguish vertebrates from invertebrates in the environment
appreciate the need to care for animals

content_topics: Parts of the human digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestines, large intestines, rectum, anus).
Healthy digestive system (dental hygiene, deworming, healthy eating).
Symptoms of unhealthy digestive system (stomach ache/pain, bloating, worms, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation).
learning_experiences: use print and non-print material to observe and identify parts of the human digestive system,
draw and label the human digestive system,
discuss symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system, record and share with peers,
collaboratively discuss and develop a plan on ways of maintaining a healthy digestive system,
use interactive platforms or digital images to illustrate the human digestive system.
key_inquiry_questions: What makes up the digestive system?
How is a healthy digestive system maintained?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to learn: The learner reflects on ways of maintaining a healthy digestive system as they develop a plan on ways of maintaining a healthy digestive system.
Digital literacy: The learner develops manipulative skills in using digital media as they use interactive platforms or digital images to illustrate the human digestive system.
sub_strands.values:
Unity: The learner strives to achieve a common goal of maintaining a healthy digestive system as they discuss and develop a plan on ways of maintaining a healthy digestive system.
Respect: The learner appreciates others’ opinions while discussing the symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system.
sub_strands.pcis: Health issues: The learner practices how to observe and maintain healthy digestive system such as dental hygiene, regular deworming and healthy eating as they plan on ways of maintaining a healthy digestive system.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner studies ways of maintaining a healthy digestive system in personal hygiene and hygienic handling of food.

outcomes.text: identify parts of the human digestive system
develop a plan of maintaining a healthy human digestive system
appreciate the importance of a healthy human digestive system

content_topics: Meaning of matter
States of matter (solid, liquid and gas).
Properties of matter (shape, volume and mass).
Importance of the different states of matter.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of matter and identify its different states,,
collect and group different substances from the environment into the three states of matter collaboratively,
carry out activities to demonstrate the properties of the three states of matter with peers,
discuss the importance of the different states of matter in day-to-day life,
use digital or print media to search for more information on the characteristics of the three states of matter.
key_inquiry_questions: What are the properties of matter?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Communication and collaboration: The learner shares different roles as they works with peers to collect and group different substances from the environment into the three states of matter and carry out activities that show properties of matter.
Digital literacy: The learner develops digital manipulative skills as they interact with digital technology to observe the properties of the three states of matter.
sub_strands.values: Unity: The learner shares available resources amicably as they carry out activities to demonstrate the properties of the three states of matter with peers.
sub_strands.pcis: Heath issues -preventive health: The learner practices preventive health measures such as avoiding blowing air into the same balloon with others as they carry out activities to demonstrate the properties of the three states of matter with peers.
sub_strands.links: Mathematics: The learner uses the knowledge of properties of matter to measure the volume and mass of different substances.

outcomes.text: categorise substances in the environment into the three states of matter
describe the properties of the three states of matter
appreciate the importance of the different states of matter in day-to-day life

content_topics: Types of solid wastes (decomposing and non-decomposing (plastic, metals, food wrappers, kitchen waste).
Dangers of solid waste to the environment.
Managing wastes in places (classrooms, schools, home, public functions).
Methods of managing solid waste (reuse, reduce and recycle).
Safety measures during solid waste management (wearing protective gear and use of appropriate tools).
learning_experiences: walk around the school compound and its environment to identify solid waste in the environment,
discuss with peers the meaning of decomposable and non-decomposable solid waste,
collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing,
discuss the dangers of solid waste to the environment and present in class,

discuss methods of managing different types of waste in their environment (To include Re-using, Recycling and Reducing), Hint: Include common waste in school and environment such as kitchen, animal waste, plastics, e-waste, metals and glasses,
practice observe proper safety measures in solid waste management
use digital or print media to search for more information on ways of managing different types of solid waste.
key_inquiry_questions: How is solid waste dangerous to the environment?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner reflects and practices good ways of managing different types of waste in their environment as they collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing.
Learning to learn: The learner explores ways of making dustbins, toys or ornaments from locally available materials
sub_strands.values:
Responsibility: The learner plays different roles from other peers as they use locally available materials to make dustbins, toys and ornaments.
Patriotism: The learner practices carrying out community service activities as they collect solid waste in the school, sort and classify them into decomposing and non-decomposing.
sub_strands.pcis:
Health issues: The learner learns about preventive health measures as they discuss the dangers of solid waste to the environment and presents in class.
Socio-economic issues; environmental education: The learner discusses ways of managing different types of solid waste in their environment and generate outcome out of the locally available waste by making dustbins, toys and ornaments.
sub_strands.links: Creative arts: The learner uses knowledge on management of solid waste to make ornaments and dustbins.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: a line on this page ran across two columns and was cut by position.

outcomes.text: classify solid waste into decomposable and non-decomposable
describe the dangers of solid waste to the environment
apply appropriate methods to manage solid waste in the environment
appreciate the need for proper management of solid waste in the environment

content_topics: Meaning of water conservation.
Methods of conserving water (cover: Simple examples of Reducing water wastage, Reusing water and Recycling water).
Importance of water conservation.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on how water is wasted at home and school,
discuss with peers the meaning of water conservation,
explore their locality and observe how water is conserved,
discuss with peers ways of conserving water.
discuss the importance of conserving water,
practise responsible use of water at home and school.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is it important to conserve water?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Critical thinking and Problem Solving: The learner practises responsible use of water at home and school as they explore their locality and observe how water is conserved with peers.
Citizenship: The learner identifies water wastage as a problem affecting society and sensitises the community on the importance of water conservation.
sub_strands.values: Integrity: The learner practices how use available water sparingly as they explore their locality and observe how water is conserved.
sub_strands.pcis: Socio-economic issues; financial literacy: The learner learns how to reduce cost of water by reducing water wastage as they explore their locality and observe how water is conserved.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner uses knowledge of appropriate water conservation practices in irrigation such as adopting drip irrigation and mulching.

outcomes.text: explain the meaning of water conservation in the environment
describe methods of conserving water at home and school
outline the importance of conserving water at home and school
develop interest in conserving water at home and school

content_topics: Types of forces (force of gravity and force of friction).
Effects of force on objects (change of shape, start motion, stop moving objects, increase speed, decrease speed, change direction and hold objects together).
Uses of force in day-to-day life.
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the term force as used in science,
carry out activities that demonstrate the existence of force of gravity and force of friction in nature,
carry out activities to demonstrate the effects of force on objects,
use digital or print media to search for, observe and discuss uses of force in day-to-day life,
discuss with peers ways of minimising friction between moving objects (smoothening surfaces, greasing, oiling, use of rollers, ball bearings),
discuss the applications of force of friction and force of gravity in day-to-day life.
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to learn: The learner acquires digital manipulative skills as they use digital devices to search for uses of force in day-to-day life
Communication and collaboration: The learner develops speaking and listening skills as they discuss ways of minimising friction between moving bodies.
sub_strands.values:
Love: The learner cares for one another by avoiding inflicting pain on each other or safely uses available materials as they work with peers to carry out activities that demonstrate the existence of force of gravity and force of friction in nature.
Unity: The learner practices taking turns in carrying out certain tasks as they carry out activities that demonstrate the existence of force of gravity and force of friction in nature.
sub_strands.pcis: Citizenship: The learner exercises leadership as they work in groups while discussing the application of force of friction and force of gravity in day-to-day life.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner relates the concepts of force of friction in maintenance farm tools and equipment.

outcomes.text: describe types of forces in nature
demonstrate the effects of force on objects in nature
describe the uses of force in daily life
appreciate the importance of force in day-to-day life

content_topics: Sources of light.
Ways of lighting the house (windows, translucent roofs, artificial lighting).
Uses of light (to see, safety, discourage pests).
learning_experiences: brainstorm on the meaning of light,
carry out activities to categorise the sources of light in day-to-day life as natural or artificial,
discuss with peers the ways of lighting a house,
use digital or print media to search for information on sources and uses of light in nature,
discuss with peers the applications of light in day-to-day life.
key_inquiry_questions: Why is light important in day-to-day life?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Digital literacy: The learner acquires digital manipulative skills as they interact with technology to search for sources and uses of light in nature.
Communication and Collaboration: The learner contributes to group decision making as they discuss with peers the ways of lighting a house.
sub_strands.values: Respect: The learner exercises patience with others opinions as they discuss the applications of light in day-to-day life.
sub_strands.pcis: Citizenship education: The learner reflects and recorgnise the uses of light for safety and security as they discuss the importance of light.
sub_strands.links: Pre-technical Studies: The learner seeks alternative cost-effective ways of lighting a house as they discuss ways of lighting a house.

outcomes.text: identify the sources of light in nature
describe ways of lighting a house in day- to-day life
explain the uses of light in day-to-day life
appreciate the applications of light in day-to-day life

content_topics: Sources of heat (sun, fire, electricity).
Uses of heat (Cooking, warming, ironing and drying).
Safety measures when handling heat
Importance of heat in daily life.
learning_experiences: use digital or print media to search for the meaning of heat,
discuss with peers the sources of heat in nature,
carry out activities to demonstrate the uses of heat in day-to-day life,
discuss safety measures when using heat,
use digital or print media to search for information on safety measures and practices necessary when using heat,
discuss the importance of heat in nature.
key_inquiry_questions: What are the safety measures observed when using heat?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Learning to learn: The learner gets new information on safety measures as they digital or print media to search for information on safety measures and practices necessary when using heat.
Digital literacy: The learner develops digital manipulative skills when interacting with digital media to search for safety measures and practices necessary when using heat.
sub_strands.values: Unity: The learner practices sharing available resources amicably as they carry out activities to demonstrate the uses of heat in day-to-day life.
sub_strands.pcis: Socio-Economic Issues: The learner exercises safety and security as they carry out activities to demonstrate the uses of heat in day-to-day life.
sub_strands.links: Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner uses knowledge of heat in hatching of chicks, pest control and cooking utensils.

outcomes.text: identify sources of heat in nature
demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life
describe safety measures to observe when using heat
appreciate the importance of heat in day-to-day life

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify characteristics of plants and animals.

levels.EE: The learner accurately identifies all characteristics in plants and animals giving illustrations.
levels.ME: The learner accurately identifies all characteristics of plants and animals.
levels.AE: The learner accurately identifies most of the characteristics of plants and animals.
levels.BE: The learner identifies a few characteristics of either plants or animals.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe functions of external parts of a plant.

levels.EE: The learner correctly and comprehensively describes functions of external parts of a plant.,
levels.ME: The learner correctly describes functions of external parts of a plant.
levels.AE: The learner partially describes functions of external parts of a plant.
levels.BE: The learner describes functions of external parts of a plant with prompt.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify parts of the human digestive system.

levels.EE: The learner identifies all parts of the human digestive system correctly giving illustrations.
levels.ME: The learner identifies all parts of the human digestive system correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies most parts of the human digestive system.
levels.BE: The learner identifies a few parts of the human digestive system.

indicators.indicator: Ability to develop a plan of maintaining a healthy human digestive system.

levels.EE: The learner correctly and innovatively develops a plan of maintaining a healthy human digestive system.
levels.ME: The learner correctly develops a plan of maintaining a healthy human digestive system.
levels.AE: The learner partially develops a plan of maintaining a healthy human digestive system.
levels.BE: The learner develops a plan of maintaining a healthy human digestive system given hints.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe the properties of the three states of matter.

levels.EE: The learner describes the properties of the three states of matter correctly, giving examples from the locality.
levels.ME: The learner describes the properties of the three states of matter correctly.
levels.AE: The learner describes the properties of two of the three states of matter correctly.
levels.BE: The learner describes the properties of one of the three states of matter correctly.

indicators.indicator: Ability to manage solid waste in the environment.

levels.EE: The learner manages solid waste in the environment properly and actively engages in promoting reuse, reduce, recycle activities.
levels.ME: The learner manages solid waste in the environment properly.
levels.AE: The learner partially manages solid waste in the environment.
levels.BE: The learner manages solid waste in the environment with help.

indicators.indicator: Ability to outline the importance of conserving water at home and school.

levels.EE: The learner outlines the importance of conserving water at home and school giving examples from the locality.
levels.ME: The learner outlines the importance of conserving water at home and school.
levels.AE: The learner outlines a few the importance of conserving water at home and school.
levels.BE: The learner outlines the importance of conserving water at home or school with prompt.

indicators.indicator: Ability to demonstrate the effects of force on objects in nature.

levels.EE: The learner demonstrates the effects of force on objects in nature correctly and helps others.
levels.ME: The learner demonstrates the effects of force on objects in nature correctly.
levels.AE: The learner partially demonstrates the effects of force on objects in nature correctly.
levels.BE: The learner demonstrates the effects of force on objects in nature even, given hints.

indicators.indicator: Ability to identify the sources of light in nature.

levels.EE: The learner identifies the sources of light in nature correctly and exhaustively.
levels.ME: The learner identifies the sources of light in nature correctly.
levels.AE: The learner identifies some of the sources of light in nature correctly.
levels.BE: The learner struggles to identify the sources of light in nature even with hints.

indicators.indicator: Ability to explain the uses of light in day-to-day life.

levels.EE: The learner correctly and comprehensively explains the uses of light in day-to-day life correctly and comprehensively.
levels.ME: The learner explains the uses of light in day-to-day life correctly.
levels.AE: The learner explains most of the uses of light in day-to-day life correctly.
levels.BE: The learner explains a few uses of light in day-to-day life even.

indicators.indicator: Ability to demonstrate uses of heat in day-to-day life.

levels.EE: The learner demonstrates uses of heat in day-to-day life correctly and helps others.
levels.ME: The learner demonstrates uses of heat in day-to-day life correctly.
levels.AE: The learner demonstrates most of the uses of heat in day-to-day life correctly.
levels.BE: The learner demonstrates a few uses of heat in day-to-day life even with help.

indicators.indicator: Ability to describe safety measures when using heat.

levels.EE: The learner describes safety measures when using heat correctly and comprehensively.
levels.ME: The learner describes safety measures when using heat correctly.
levels.AE: The learner describes most of the safety measures when using heat correctly.
levels.BE: The learner describes a few safety measures when using heat correctly even with help.
